entries.subject: Calibrated Giotto HMC hmc01814
entries.finding: The retained intake identifies hmc01814 (image 3436) and its calibration. It does not establish the Stooke model-to-inertial attitude or a surface coverage mask. Derived-asset reuse also remains unresolved between the cited distribution statements; no surface texture from this frame is qualified. The complete 68-frame clear-C intake now independently matches this frame to the archive index and records the decoded sampling and actual source identities; it does not resolve the registration or reuse conditions.
entries.revisitWhen: A camera tied to the exact shape frame and an independently checked nucleus mask qualify its surface placement, and the applicable derived-image reuse terms are resolved.

entries.subject: PDS4 Stooke historical shape
entries.finding: The selected 5-degree radius grid uses east-positive longitude and the long axis as its reference axis. Published absolute uncertainty is about 0.5–1 km; its depressions may be exaggerated. The fixed display attitude is illustrative.

entries.subject: Stooke and Abergel 1991 Table 1 and Table 2
entries.finding: The separate 10-degree radius table uses a different rotation-axis frame. Its camera geometry cannot be assigned to the later PDS long-axis model without a demonstrated transformation; the paper also reports limb and terminator mismatches. Full-paper inspection on 27 September confirmed that Table 2 is a separate 10-degree radius model and Table 3 locates features by the same model graticules. No numerical transcription or projection trial was performed; the incompatibility finding remains.
entries.revisitWhen: An exact version and coordinate transformation binds those cameras to their matching shape or to the selected PDS model.

entries.subject: Revised model described in the 1995 LPSC abstract
entries.finding: The two-page abstract describes a revised slow long-axis model, but provides neither numerical camera controls nor a radius table. Its shared Belton citation does not establish exact identity with the selected PDS version.
entries.revisitWhen: The revised numerical shape and camera or frame records become available.

entries.subject: MPS Giotto composite region
entries.finding: The displayed composite region is retained with approximate encounter projection and the MPS educational-use attribution record. The held-out silhouette check tests outline consistency, not independent internal feature locations.

entries.subject: Processed Vega 2 T11190 and T11194
entries.finding: The two processed images extend the existing Giotto + Vega lens while preserving all previously accepted Giotto map pixels. The relative Vega display gain passes held-out overlap checks; cross-filter brightness is not recovered albedo.

entries.subject: Independent Halley feature registration
entries.finding: The source-and-evidence record defers photographic faithfulness because silhouette agreement does not independently establish interior feature coordinates on this uncertain historical mesh. The Historical model remains the supported shape view. Full clear-C intake and recovered 1991 feature tables do not supply independent controls in the selected long-axis model frame.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent surface features with a verified model frame validate the photographic placement within stated source uncertainty.

entries.subject: Public rotation compilation and Vega ephemerides
entries.finding: The 2004 rotation compilation and mission ephemerides support the approximate projection. Rounded rotation parameters, 148 seconds of observer extrapolation and a single camera for a composite remain limitations; no current tumbling state is inferred.

entries.subject: Reitsema, Delamere and Keller 1989 feature catalog
entries.finding: Reitsema feature coordinates are reproduced in Stooke and Abergel (1991), Table 3. The paper describes their frame as a two-dimensional ellipse with non-planetocentric latitudes, so an approximate longitude offset is not a full coordinate conversion. The neighboring Stooke coordinates come from model graticules and are not independent 3D controls. Original Reitsema full text and a binding to the selected PDS shape remain unresolved.
entries.revisitWhen: The feature coordinates and their original frame can be retrieved and matched to the chosen model.

entries.subject: Belton 1991 rotation solution
entries.finding: The shape label and later public compilation cite this solution, but the full original tables were not established as a directly consumed camera-to-shape source. The public compilation supports the current approximation.
entries.revisitWhen: The original tables can be checked against the selected model version and public compilation.

entries.subject: MPS catalog figures 55, 63 and 66
entries.finding: These presentations of the close-up region were inspected without establishing an independently qualified extension of the accepted footprint. The new inspection of figure 66 confirms that it is a set of enhanced close-up crops, not a controlled surface map. No new coverage has been qualified.
entries.revisitWhen: A distinct photographed region and independent registration demonstrate useful new coverage.

entries.subject: IKF transformations of Vega T11190
entries.finding: These products are transformations of the same observation and add no new viewing geometry. Their copyrighted processed images were not used.
entries.revisitWhen: A distinct observation adds useful geometry and its processing and reuse rights are established.

entries.subject: Cross-mission Giotto/Vega brightness gain
entries.finding: Only six distinct overlap blocks were available, so the cross-mission gain was rejected. Giotto retains its original RGB; the independently supported Vega-to-Vega gain is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: Adequate independent cross-mission overlap supports a bounded gain without changing the meaning of the mixed-filter photographs.

entries.subject: Complete Giotto clear-C close-approach sequence
entries.finding: The diagnostic consumes all 68 sensor-C CLEAR multi-detector frames and checks their dimensions, timing and superpixel factors against the native indexes. All rasters were visually inspected with independent percentile stretches. This is diagnostic inclusion only: no new photographic surface is qualified.

entries.subject: Larger intermediate encounter maps
entries.finding: On 3,830 common interior points, area-weighted mean absolute display-byte error falls from 0.406 at width 512 to 0.194 at width 2048. This small resampling gain does not establish recovered surface detail. Seams, missing regions, final atlas rendering and registration accuracy are outside the measurement; the delivered map remains unchanged.
entries.revisitWhen: A matched measurement demonstrates useful detail or seam improvement in the final rendered atlas under a qualified registration.

entries.subject: Newly processed Giotto figure published in 2017
entries.finding: Figure 8a in Ksanfomality (2017) was inspected from the publisher PDF. It is a new processing of Giotto imagery; the paper warns of possible artifacts in its smallest details. It supplies no numerical camera-to-shape registration or standalone calibrated raster. Reference 19 points to a Venera processing study whose full text was unavailable. No new texture is qualified.
entries.revisitWhen: A reproducible Halley input and processing record, usable raster and reuse terms, and independent surface registration establish the added information.

entries.subject: Szego et al. 2001 rotation and outgassing model
entries.finding: Our OpenAlex query returned the paper and its abstract, including a potential alternative rotation and shape-model route. The publisher and ADS PDFs returned HTTP 403. The original numerical solution and its compatibility with the selected PDS shape were not examined; lack of access does not exclude the model.
entries.revisitWhen: The primary full text and numerical model can be read and matched to the observation and shape frames.

entries.subject: Spherical-harmonic Halley shape in coma modelling
entries.finding: Marschall et al. (2020), section 3, identifies a Halley shape derived from Giotto and Vega observations in Crifo et al. (2002), Challenging a paradigm. The original numerical coefficients, model frame and primary 2002 full text were not recovered. This is a candidate model route, not evidence of a better released mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: The original numerical shape and frame are recovered and tested against held-out imagery with their stated uncertainty.

entries.subject: 2015 reanalysis of the 1985/86 lightcurve
entries.finding: The abstract and sections 1–3.3 provide additional time-dependent constraints on complex rotation; section 1 describes a nucleus model as subsequent work. These results can constrain a future orientation fit, but no camera-to-selected-shape solution was established in this inspection.
entries.revisitWhen: A released orientation solution or an independently checked fit uses these lightcurves to establish the exact model phase and observation cameras.

entries.subject: 2025 Halley rendezvous mission proposal
entries.finding: The proposed 2061-return mission motivates new shape and rotation measurements. It does not supply a newly observed nucleus surface release and cannot replace current source imagery.
entries.revisitWhen: A mission releases actual observations or a reproducible numerical model useful to the nucleus dataset.

entries.subject: JWST as a source for a resolved Halley surface
entries.finding: At a representative observer distance of 35 AU, a 15 km nucleus spans about 0.00059 arcsec, far below NIRCam FWHM of approximately 0.07 arcsec at 2 micrometres. The paper API query failed with a rate limit and fallback timeout; actual JWST observations were not established or ruled out. Unresolved photometry and spectroscopy cannot provide this surface texture.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation resolves the nucleus with enough spatial sampling and geometry to test a surface product.
